speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; how long has this been present and have you noticed any specific triggers like new soaps, plants, or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history. Given the chronic nature of this pruritic rash on your upper extremities lasting five months, have you noticed any pattern with heat, sweating, or stress? Additionally, I need to examine the rash itself; please lift your arms so I can look, and if you have any recent images of it, please share them.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Prurigo Pigmentosa.

The combination of a persistent, pruritic rash on the upper extremities lasting five months, in the absence of fever, joint pain, or systemic illness, is highly characteristic of Prurigo Pigmentosa, a condition often associated with underlying neurological or psychiatric disorders.
